messages:
maria.gomez: Heads-up — planning a canary rollout for feature-x at 10:35 PT. Quick question: who is allowed to flip the emergency toggle for this feature if we see a spike?

sam_kim: I figured eng-oncall + infra leads + SRE oncall. Is there an official short list? don't want product folks accidentally flipping in panic.

priya: Policy summary from runbook: only eng-oncall rotation, eng-infra-leads, and SRE-oncall can do emergency flips. Any flip must include an audit reason and link to the incident ticket. Snippet:
```
- Who: eng-oncall, eng-infra-lead, SRE-oncall
- How: /ops toggle feature-x off --audit="reason"
- Slack notify: #incidents (auto)
```

alex: Quick technical q — does the /ops toggle require 2FA or is SSO enough? If it's just SSO we should require an explicit audit string and a follow-up ticket by the flipper.

ops-bot: reminder: All /ops toggle commands create an immutable audit entry with executor, timestamp, and the raw command. See https://internal.redwood/wikis/ops-toggle for details.

maria.gomez: Good. Also proposing guardrails: automated soft-throttle when error-rate spikes above 5% for >1m. Full kill (toggle off) is manual only after oncall confirms.

sam_kim: And the person who flips should be listed as postmortem owner by default. Otherwise we have handoff ambiguity.

priya: Agree. We can enforce adding `postmortem_owner=@who_flipped` in the audit note. ops-bot will auto-create a ticket when that tag is present.

alex: Can the toggle command also capture the git sha and rollout percentage? That info would be super helpful for triage.

priya: Filing a tiny enhancement: ENG-2345 to add git sha + rollout pct to audit metadata.

maria.gomez: For this canary: I'll start at 10:35 and ramp to 10% over 10m. If error-rate >3% or latency p95 degrades >200ms, we stop and escalate.

sam_kim: Which PagerDuty escalation should fire for canary regressions? We need a clear channel.

priya: Use the 'feature-x-canary' PD service — it alerts eng-oncall -> infra lead. I'll add the saturation thresholds to the PD policy.

alex: I'll be on standby to flip if we see the threshold and pager fires. I'll also paste the exact /ops command in here once ready.

ops-bot: policy note: toggle commands executed by non-authorized accounts will be rejected and logged. Rejected attempts are also added to the audit feed.

maria.gomez: After the canary, whoever flipped or confirmed success should post a short status and the audit command output to #eng-postmortems. That keeps one record.

sam_kim: tiny nit: can we have the toggle CLI remind authors to include a short rollback plan in the audit string? e.g., `--audit="reason; rollback: revert-commit-abc123"`

priya: Good idea. Adding to ENG-2345. Also creating a runbook blurb for this exact flow so oncall can step through quickly.

alex: Command i'll run if needed: `/ops toggle feature-x off --audit="canary spike 2026-03-17; postmortem_owner=@alex; rollback: revert abc123"`

maria.gomez: Perfect. Everyone set for 10:35? please ack.

sam_kim: ack

priya: ack, I'll watch logs and PD.

alex: ack, standing by.

maria.gomez: rolling at 10:35 — will update this thread after 11:00 with outcomes. :thumbsup:
